blocks: Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on Strengthening the Protection of Online Information
(Adopted at the 30th session of the Standing Committee of the Eleventh National People’s Congress on 28 December 2012)

In order to protect the security of online information, to safeguard the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons and other organisations, and to safeguard national security and the public interest, the following decision is made:
I. The State protects electronic information capable of identifying the personal identity of a citizen and electronic information concerning a citizen’s personal privacy.
No organisation or individual may steal, or obtain by other unlawful means, a citizen’s personal electronic information, and none may sell or unlawfully provide such information to others.

II. Where network service providers and other enterprises and institutions collect or use a citizen’s personal electronic information in the course of their business activities, they shall follow the principles of lawfulness, legitimacy and necessity, shall expressly state the purpose, means and scope of the collection and use, and shall obtain the consent of the person from whom the information is collected; they may not collect or use the information in contravention of laws and regulations or of what the two parties have agreed.
Where network service providers and other enterprises and institutions collect or use a citizen’s personal electronic information, they shall make public their rules for such collection and use.

III. Network service providers and other enterprises and institutions, and their staff, must keep strictly confidential the personal electronic information of citizens collected in the course of their business activities; they may not disclose, tamper with or damage it, and may not sell it or unlawfully provide it to others.

IV. Network service providers and other enterprises and institutions shall adopt technical and other necessary measures to ensure information security and to prevent the disclosure, damage or loss of personal electronic information of citizens collected in the course of their business activities. Where disclosure, damage or loss occurs or may occur, remedial measures shall be taken immediately.

V. A network service provider shall strengthen the management of information published by its users; on discovering information whose publication or transmission is prohibited by laws or regulations, it shall immediately cease transmitting that information, take measures such as removal, preserve the relevant records, and report to the competent authorities.

VI. Where a network service provider arranges website access services for a user, handles the formalities for network access for a fixed-line telephone, mobile telephone or the like, or provides a user with information publication services, it shall require the user to provide genuine identity information at the time the agreement with the user is signed or the provision of the service is confirmed.

VII. No organisation or individual may send commercial electronic information to a recipient’s fixed-line telephone, mobile telephone or personal email address without the recipient’s consent or request, or where the recipient has expressly refused it.

VIII. A citizen who finds online information that infringes their lawful rights and interests, such as the disclosure of their personal identity or the dissemination of their personal privacy, or who is harassed by commercial electronic information, has the right to require the network service provider to delete the information concerned or to take other necessary measures to stop it.

IX. Any organisation or individual has the right to report or lodge a complaint with the competent authorities concerning unlawful or criminal conduct consisting of stealing, or obtaining by other unlawful means, selling or unlawfully providing to others a citizen’s personal electronic information, and concerning other unlawful or criminal conduct relating to online information; the authority receiving the report or complaint shall deal with it promptly in accordance with law. The injured party may bring an action in accordance with law.

X. The competent authorities shall perform their duties in accordance with law within the scope of their respective powers, and shall adopt technical and other necessary measures to prevent, stop and investigate unlawful or criminal conduct consisting of stealing, or obtaining by other unlawful means, selling or unlawfully providing to others a citizen’s personal electronic information, and other unlawful or criminal conduct relating to online information. Where a competent authority performs its duties in accordance with law, network service providers shall cooperate with it and provide technical support.

State organs and their staff shall keep confidential the personal electronic information of citizens that comes to their knowledge in the performance of their duties; they may not disclose, tamper with or damage it, and may not sell it or unlawfully provide it to others.

XI. Conduct in violation of this Decision shall be subject, in accordance with law, to penalties including a warning, a fine, confiscation of unlawful gains, revocation of a licence or cancellation of a filing, closure of the website, and prohibition of the responsible persons from engaging in the network service business; such penalties shall be recorded in social credit files and made public. Where the conduct constitutes a violation of public security administration, a public security administrative penalty shall be imposed in accordance with law. Where it constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with law. Where it infringes the civil rights and interests of another, civil liability shall be borne in accordance with law.
XII. This Decision takes effect from the date of its promulgation.
